candidates.explanation: I couldn't see this file, so the location is a best guess from the project's usual structure. The photo-handling block in update() most likely sets the local `photo` variable to `null` when the payload has no `photo` field. It should stay `undefined` in that case. The value is then spread into the repository update, which overwrites the stored photo with null. A partial update such as one that changes only firstName therefore clears the avatar. Only an explicit `photo: null` should clear it, and only a payload with `photo.id` should replace it.

Also a guess. If toPersistence builds `photo` as null or an empty entity whenever `domainEntity.photo` is undefined, the repository's save/merge writes a null photo relation. The mapper should leave the photo property undefined when the domain object doesn't carry one.

Also a guess. The /auth/me PATCH handler may rebuild or default `userDto.photo` when the request doesn't include it. It should pass the DTO through unchanged, so that `photo` stays undefined when omitted.

fix.description: In UsersService.update, initialize `photo` as `undefined`, not `null`. Set it to the found file only when `clonedPayload.photo?.id` is present. Set it to `null` only when `clonedPayload.photo === null` (an explicit removal). Make sure the repository update and mapper skip `photo` when it is undefined, so a partial update such as firstName alone leaves the avatar unchanged.
